ground_truth: Well, the drive to form my own firm was really sort of an accident, like a lot of things in life. I was quite happy at [financial firm A]. I was head of the merger department, and we were doing an enormous number of deals. It was really an exciting place, a wonderful place. And then we got into financial difficulty, and the firm blew up, and basically I sold it to [financial firm B]. And during that process, I got to watch some truly unattractive behavior by people who were supposed to be protecting the firm, people 10 years older than me. And I decided I didn't want to stay there, and I had done a lot of work while I was at [financial firm A] with the chairman of the firm, who was a fellow named [Person A]. And [Person A] and I enjoyed working together. And [Person A] had left in a power struggle a year before we sold the firm. And so I decided that after we sold the firm that I wanted to join [Person A], and [Person A] decided he wanted to join me, and what we wanted to do was to work together again. It was sort of a logical thing to want to do with one's life, and it had a good feeling, which is sort of when you do things in life that have a good feeling, it tends to work out well, as opposed to coming up with a wonderful strategic plan. And we came up with a good strategic plan to do. Advisory work to pay the rent, to go into the buyout business, because it looked like a pretty easy way, frankly, to make money in the mid-'80s. And then the third piece of our strategic plan was to attract very gifted people who wanted to be in business with us, sort of split the ownership of that business or the profits. And that was a good strategy because Wall Street was growing so rapidly at that point that people often felt a sense of just being alienated from the firms where they grew up. When I joined [financial firm A], we had 550 people, and now any respectable securities firm has numbers in the tens of thousands. And how many does [financial firm C] have? We have 550 people. Isn't that curious? Right where I started. So, in effect, no progress was made.

background.text: So, a lot of progress was made. You may be the largest private equity firm in the country. Tell me what private equity is and what it is that you do.

ground_truth: Well, what we do is pretty simple. We raise large amounts of money from principally institutions, pension funds, endowments, and then we buy companies using those funds, and we basically borrow about $3, sometimes a little more, sometimes a little less, to every dollar of equity that we put up in the deal.
